belongs_to: Book p.72 question 'In the number line shown below, what decimal numbers do the boxes labelled a, b and c denote?' (printed answer, first picture of this page; the question version on pdf p.26 has the letters a, b, c in the boxes)
description: Horizontal number line with an arrowhead at BOTH ends, drawn in dark ink. 11 equally spaced vertical tick marks (counted), tick 1 at the left and tick 11 at the right; the line extends a little more than one tick-gap beyond the first and the last tick before each arrowhead. Labels under the ticks: '5' under tick 1 (leftmost) and '10' under tick 11 (rightmost); no other tick is labelled. Unit step = 0.5 (so ticks read 5, 5.5, 6, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8, 8.5, 9, 9.5, 10). Three ticks are extended downwards into long vertical arrows ending in arrowheads that point down into the top edge of a square box: the arrow from tick 3 points into a box containing '6'; the arrow from tick 6 points into a box containing '7.5'; the arrow from tick 10 points into a box containing '9.5'. Boxes are empty-white squares with a dark outline, each drawn directly below its arrow, all at the same height, not touching each other; the numbers inside are RED (the printed answers) and the box numbers are the only red items. In the question version these boxes show the letters a (tick 3), b (tick 6) and c (tick 10) instead of values.

belongs_to: Book p.73 Math Talk 'In each case below use the digits 4, 1, 8, 2, and 5 exactly once and try to make a decimal number as close as possible to 25' (printed answer; the question on pdf p.28 shows the same three rows of EMPTY coloured boxes)
description: Three rows of square digit tiles, stacked vertically, each tile a square with a dark outline and a black digit in the middle, and a small black dot (decimal point) at the baseline between two tiles; the three decimal points sit exactly above one another (rows are aligned on the decimal point, so the rows are shifted left/right). Row 1 (top) = 5 GREEN tiles: '2' '5' . '1' '4' '8' (2 tiles before the point, 3 after) = 25.148. Row 2 (middle) = 4 YELLOW tiles: '8' . '5' '4' '2' (1 tile before the point, 3 after) = 8.542; this is the shortest row and begins to the right of rows 1 and 3; its '8' tile stands directly under the '5' tile of row 1 and above the '4' tile of row 3 (the three tiles just before the point form one column). Row 3 (bottom) = 5 PINK tiles: '1' '2' '4' . '5' '8' (3 tiles before the point, 2 after) = 124.58, it extends furthest to the left. All digits are black (no red). In total 14 tiles.
unclear: The yellow row has only 4 tiles (8.542) so the digit 1 is not used in that row; this is exactly what the book prints (the question's empty yellow row also has 4 boxes), not a reading problem.

belongs_to: Book p.80 Figure it Out question 15 'Using each digit 0-9 not more than once, fill the boxes below so that the sum is closest to 10.5' (printed answer picture; the question version on pdf p.35 shows the same boxes empty and no result row)
description: A vertical addition of two decimal numbers made of yellow square tiles. Top row: 4 yellow square tiles with dark outline holding RED digits '9' . '4' '7' '6' (one tile before a black decimal point, three after) = 9.476. Second row: a black '+' sign to the left, then 4 yellow tiles with RED digits '1' . '0' '2' '5' = 1.025; the two rows are aligned column by column and on the decimal points (tile columns: 1 before the point, then 3 after). Below the rows a long black horizontal rule spanning the full width. Under the rule, in small BLACK digits, the sum written column by column: '10' under the first tile column, '.' under the decimal points, '5' under the first tile after the point, '0' under the second, '1' under the third, i.e. 10.501 (the '10' is two digits written under the one wide column of the units tile). 8 tiles in total; digits used 9,4,7,6,1,0,2,5 (each once; 3 and 8 unused). Red = the filled-in answer, black = the sum line.
